t: Great match at cricket in Calais
c: In 1769, the Whitehall Evening Post reported that a "great match at Cricket" was to be played at Calais in northern France.

t: British cricket clubs established in Calcutta
c: British clubs were established in India in Calcutta (1792) and, following the siege there, Seringapatam (1799).

t: William Pitt references cricket in Commons
c: In 1803, William Pitt referred to cricket when the Commons debated the Defence Bill that was later passed into law as the Defence of the Realm Act 1803.

t: Cricket recovery as Napoleonic Wars end
c: A discernible recovery began in 1815 as the Napoleonic Wars ended after the Battle of Waterloo on 18 June.

t: Lord relocates turf to Middle Ground

t: Parliament requisitions Middle Ground for Regent's Canal
c: In 1813, the site of the Middle Ground was requisitioned by Parliament for construction of the Regent's Canal.

t: Thomas Boxall publishes cricket instructional book

c: The first of these was the All England Eleven(the AEE), founded by William Clarke in 1846 and then managed by George Parr following Clarke's death.

c: The rival United All England Eleven (the UEE) was established by Jemmy Dean and John Wisden in 1852.

t: Lord's hosts last Public Schools Weeks
c: Lord's hosted the last Public Schools Weeks (Eton, Harrow, and Winchester) in 1854.

t: Eyre Estate sells Lord's freehold to Isaac Moses
c: The Eyre Estate sold the freehold of Lord's to Isaac Moses, a property trader, at public auction in 1860 for £7,000.

t: MCC acquires leasehold from James Dark
c: James Dark held the leasehold until 1864, when he ceded it to MCC, who afterwards purchased the freehold from Mr Moses at a substantial profit.
